body:
Settles both questions F-7a530b left open. OBSERVED on PR #1604, run
31809460486 (2026-08-14), from the `cwn-e2e-logs` artifact — which F-7a530b
said was never captured, but the "Dump container logs" step has been
`if: always()` since then (`.github/workflows/tests.yml`). That part of
F-7a530b is stale; the evidence is there, nobody had pulled it.

## Q1 — did the container crash? No.

- `Starting Gevent server on [::]:8083` appears exactly **once**, 14:29:24.
- The same process is still logging at **14:35:38**, six minutes later.
- No traceback anywhere in the request path. The only recurring exception is
  an unrelated `ModuleNotFoundError: No module named 'scripts'` in
  `cps/api/duplicates.py:45`, which returns a handled 500 and does not stop
  the server.

So the harness lost the socket while the server was *starved*, not because it
died. "socket hang up" here means "did not answer in time", not "crashed".

## Q2 — is tag mutation causal or coincidental? Causal, indirectly.

`metadata-change-detector` spawns a **fresh Python process per change-log
file**, and each one imports the whole `cps` package — that is what every
`INFO {cps:90} ProxyFix configured...` line is. 37 change-logs in a ~6 minute
run.

Spawns per minute, against the failure times:

| minute | spawns |
|---|---|
| 14:29 | 10 |
| 14:31 | 2 |
| **14:33** | **16** |
| 14:34 | 7 |
| 14:35 | 6 |

The spec failed at **14:33:06.4**, retried at **14:33:13.5** and **14:33:17.5**
— all three inside the single busiest spawn minute of the run. A spawn is
logged at 14:33:06.379, 30 ms before the first failure, and two more land
54 ms apart at 14:33:17.645/.699 around retry 2. One of those spawned
processes then ran migrations at 14:33:18 (`annotation-decouple-migration`,
`Migrating system magic shelves`, creating 5 magic shelves for user 3) —
heavy SQLite work in a forked process.

The mechanism, and why this spec: mutating specs generate metadata
change-logs. `tag-merge-delete` mints and deletes tags, and a shelf delete is
logged at 14:33:03, three seconds before the failure. The mutation *creates*
the storm that then starves the server it is about to query. The spec is both
trigger and victim, which is why it flakes far more than its neighbours while
a data-and-docs-only PR (#1434) could also trip it.

This compounds with the known gevent constraint: this build runs **no**
`monkey.patch_all()`, so blocking work does not yield the hub. A CPU-saturated
2-core runner plus a fork storm is enough to make the listener miss a
connection without any crash to show for it.

## Direction

Do not quarantine — the spec is honest and the defect it points at is real.
Fix the trigger, in `metadata-change-detector`: coalesce change-logs into one
batch pass instead of one process per file, and/or debounce, and/or cap
concurrent spawns to 1. 16 full `cps` imports in a minute is the actual bug;
the flaky spec is only the messenger.

Not yet established: whether a spawn cap alone removes the flake, and whether
the same storm explains the other clustered flakes F-7a530b listed
(`reader-rtl`, `sp1-ux`).
title: e2e 'socket hang up' is metadata-change-detector spawn storm starving gevent, not a crash
